label: Q3 2026
headline: Gross margin is back, profit isn't: the money is going into AI and robots

points.t: Gross margin recovered, but deliveries are still −2% y/y.
Operating income −56% y/y, GAAP EPS only $0.22.
Expected to turn negative for the year, it came in positive, and the capex guide was cut.

reaction: Stock: turned lower after the call and closed −3.1% the next day. Expectations use FactSet consensus; revenue consensus across sources ranges from $27.78B to $28.44B.

volprice.title: Auto revenue = deliveries × revenue per vehicle
volprice.take: In autos, both volume and price slipped slightly; the gross margin improvement came from costs and regional mix, not from selling more or at higher prices.
volprice.note: Revenue per vehicle = total auto revenue ÷ deliveries; auto revenue includes leasing and regulatory credits, so it is approximate.

segments.title: By business
segments.take: “Flat” revenue is one gain offsetting two declines: services and other grew 33%, while autos and storage both fell.

rows.why: Gross margin 15.9%, a record. The only business clearly growing.
Gross margin 18.1% (excluding credits), versus 15.4% a year ago.
Deployments +10% but revenue −16%, partly because of tariff refunds.

segments.note: Tesla does not disclose segment operating income. Services and other includes Superchargers, insurance, used cars and Robotaxi.

trends.why: Gross margin gains eaten by operating expenses
Up this quarter, still below a year ago
Negative in Q2, unexpectedly positive in Q3
−2% y/y; demand hasn't returned to growth

valuation.take: On GAAP earnings the stock is about 412x trailing profit, and still 218x on the company's measure. This price is not for the car business; it is for whether Robotaxi and Optimus deliver.

history.title: Against its own last 5 years
history.note: 14.2x now is above 14 of the last 20 quarter ends, the 70th percentile; median 10.7x. This chart uses StockAnalysis data, slightly different from the 12.8x above.

sotp.title: Sum of the parts: how much the market pays for the “future”
sotp.intro: Value today's businesses at peer multiples; what's left is what the market pays for Robotaxi, Optimus and other businesses with no revenue yet.
sotp.note: For reference: Toyota trades at 1.4x EV/revenue, storage company Fluence at 0.4x. The defaults already give Tesla a clear premium. Segment revenue is the sum of the last four quarters.

cash.title: The real cost of stock compensation
cash.note: The stock given to employees over the past year was worth 30% more than the free cash flow the company generated. Non-GAAP profit and adjusted EBITDA both exclude this cost. Quarterly stock comp was +76% y/y.

TTM earnings

decomp.note: On GAAP, trailing profit fell 16% while the stock fell only 3%, so the market actually paid a higher multiple: investors are paying for the future, not for this quarter.

calc: Cash and short-term investments $45.4B, debt and finance leases $9.5B → EV $1,290.5B
TTM = Q4'25 to Q3'26: revenue $103.57B, GAAP EPS $0.91, non-GAAP EPS $1.72, adjusted EBITDA $15.0B, FCF $3.30B
valuation.next: TSLA's profits are too thin for a guidance-based forward P/E or three scenarios to mean much, so this page leaves them out.

items: Robotaxi driverless miles grew 8x this quarter
FSD take rate on new North American cars above 75% (about 55% last quarter)
Megapack capacity nearly sold out through 2027
Deliberately cooled expectations for Optimus: the ramp will be bumpy
Robotaxi cost per mile: target $0.30, not yet reached
Optimus unit cost: declined to give a number
